title: The Birthday Pencil
moral: Kindness can make someone feel included. A small gift given with a good heart can become the beginning of friendship.

pages.text:
Maira's birthday was on Friday.

She brought a small box of pencils to class, one for each child. They were blue with tiny silver stars.

"Please take only one," she said.

Everyone came to her desk.

Aarif took one pencil and smiled. "This looks too nice for maths."

"It will still have to suffer," said Maira.

Everyone laughed.

At the end of the day, Maira looked into the box.

One pencil was left.

She counted the names in her head. Everyone had taken one.

Then she saw Renu sitting near the window, packing slowly.

Renu had joined class only that week. She was quiet and often looked unsure about where to stand or whom to talk to.

Maira walked over.

"Did you get a pencil?" she asked.

Renu shook her head.

"I thought maybe they were only for your friends."

Maira felt a little sad.

"They are for everyone," she said.

She gave Renu the last pencil.

Renu held it carefully. "Thank you."

The next Monday, Maira came to school feeling excited. She expected her friends to talk about her birthday party.

But during writing time, her own pencil broke.

She searched her pouch. No sharp pencil.

Before she could ask anyone, Renu quietly placed the blue star pencil on her desk.

"You can use it," Renu said.

Maira looked at it. "But that is your birthday pencil."

Renu smiled. "You gave it to me when I felt left out. Now it can help you too."

Maira sharpened it carefully and wrote her work.

At lunch, Renu opened her tiffin. Inside were two small pieces of cake.

"My mother made this," she said. "One is for you."

Aarif leaned over. "Does the pencil also bring cake?"

Maira laughed. "Only if you are kind to it."

Renu laughed too.

It was the first time Maira heard her laugh properly.

The blue pencil became shorter day by day, but Maira noticed something else growing.

A friendship. And it had started with one small gift given at the right time.
